enhancement_spec.status: AWAITING PRINCIPAL APPROVAL — nothing here is built until approved and routed to task 6.2

findings.finding: The tag filter is engineered well and presented expensively. Engine (assets/js/pages/home/ tagfilter.js): faceted category-AND/chip-OR matching, predictive dead-end dimming via data-empty, aria-pressed toggle chips, role="status" aria-live="polite" count line, hidden attribute keeping layout and tab order synchronized. Presentation (index.html 232–272 + work.css .tagfilter block): 13 always-visible chips at min-height 44px across 3 stacked, labeled rows, plus head row, status line, and top/bottom borders — roughly 260–330px of vertical space at every viewport, permanently expanded, to shortlist a pool of FOUR cards. The disproportion is the defect; the engine is an asset to preserve.

Home carries only hero-local CSS motion (fadeUp entrances, ambient drift, badge pulse in hero.css) plus cross-document View Transitions via assets/css/base/reset.css (@view-transition navigation:auto, with a reduced-motion suppressor). ZERO of the motion spec's named Home splice points are implemented: no S1 scroll choreography on section entrances, no S3 sequenced hero build, no S5 compositing signature, no S6 depth on work cards. The briefs, by contrast, carry a native motion layer (Brief 01's D7 layer) and the scroll-progress bar. Home is the least-animated page on a site whose motion system is itself a portfolio claim.

Scroll-progress bar: present inline on brief pages (.progress/.progress__fill, purple, reverses on upscroll, aria-hidden="true"), ABSENT on Home — the roadmap's named upgrade. Nav: shared nav.css gives Home smart hide-on-scroll (.nav--hidden translateY) + hover/focus underline + language panel; briefs replicate chrome inline. No active-section indication exists on Home's nav. Footer: present on all five pages (Home: tagline + LinkedIn CTA + meta strip); content parity across the five copies is unverified and drift-prone since briefs are self-contained.

The breakpoint grid is inconsistent across the CSS corpus: max-width 767px (10 uses) and min-width 768px (6) form the dominant mobile/desktop hinge, but variants coexist — max-width:768px (3+1), min-width:769px (2), max-width 1023px (5+2) vs max-width 1024px (1), plus strays at 900px, 641px, 480px. Off-by-one pairs (768/769, 1023/1024) create 1px bands where rules from both sides apply or neither does. Not currently a visible defect, but a latent consistency risk and the single cheapest hardening available.

Interaction organisms proven on briefs and absent on Home: expandable reveal-cards (aria-expanded + rv_btn pattern — used 8+ times across Brief 01/04 for progressive disclosure of depth), tabbed dashboards (Measured / Derived / The read), and expand-all controls (Brief 04 Gantt). These deliver the site's signature move — headline claim, voluntary depth — and Home currently has no progressive-disclosure vocabulary at all.

EN/ES voice is consistent post-task-5.6 with two logged residuals: (a) the contact_engagement_placeholder tuteo slip ("Selecciona una" amid usted register) — carried forward from 5.6 as an open item; (b) the Wave-4 logged tension between Brief 01's hero_read "5 min read" and its hero_rv_txt "the next four minutes" (EN; ES mirrors the tension as "los próximos cuatro minutos"). No new drift found.

Hero entrance animations in hero.css (fadeUp, drift, pulse) run as unconditional CSS keyframes; whether the site's global reduced-motion clamp actually covers them is not verifiable by static read alone (7 prefers-reduced-motion blocks exist across the corpus, none co-located with hero.css). Flagged for runtime verification in 6.2 rather than asserted as a defect.

proposal.title: Filter bar v2 — collapsed disclosure bar, same engine
proposal.change: Collapse the permanently-expanded three-row filter into a single resting row (~56px): left, the existing uppercase label ("Filter the work"); center, three CATEGORY DISCLOSURE TRIGGERS — "Industry", "Field", "Role" — each a button carrying aria-expanded + aria-controls and a live count badge when its category has active chips ("Field · 2"); right, the status line and Clear. Activating a trigger opens that category's chip panel directly beneath the bar (one panel at a time; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger; outside-click closes). THE CHIP ENGINE IS UNCHANGED: the same aria-pressed toggle chips, the same tagfilter.js faceted matching, dead-end dimming, live-region status — the panels simply house the chips that today sit permanently open. Active selections additionally render as removable mini-chips inline in the bar (each a button: "Banking ✕"), so the current filter state is always visible at resting height without any panel open.
proposal.rationale: Reclaims ~200–270px above the fold's work grid, converts the filter from a wall the visitor must read past into an instrument they opt into, and keeps every proven engineering behavior. Cognitive load drops because the resting state shows only what is chosen, not everything choosable. This is the disclosure grammar the briefs already taught the site (F-5), applied to Home's one overweight organism (F-1).
proposal.interaction_model: Triggers are buttons with aria-expanded/aria-controls (disclosure pattern — chosen over listbox/menu/select-multiple precisely because the payload stays ordinary toggle buttons, the most robust multi-select a11y primitive available; native select-multiple is rejected for unusable mobile UX and unstylable rendering; checkbox groups are equivalent a11y but would discard the proven chip idiom for no gain).
proposal.responsive: Desktop (min-width 768px): single-row bar, panels open as full-width strips beneath it. Mobile (max-width 767px): the three triggers remain in one horizontally-wrapping row; panels open identically; active mini-chips wrap to a second row when present. No new breakpoint introduced; uses the dominant 767/768 hinge. Resting height shrinks at every viewport; nothing overflows; 44px minimum touch targets preserved on triggers, chips, and mini-chip removers.
proposal.aa: Preserved and improved: chips keep aria-pressed; triggers add correct aria-expanded/aria-controls; focus order follows DOM (bar → open panel → grid); Escape + focus-return implemented; the existing role="status" live region continues announcing counts; mini-chip removers get accessible names ("Remove filter: Banking" via aria-label from a new i18n key). Contrast unchanged (existing token palette). Panel open/close ships a static end-state and respects reduced motion (see P-2).
proposal.i18n_keys: New CHROME keys (EN first; ES direction per designops-copy-es, final ES locks at 6.3): filter_remove_label ("Remove filter: {tag}" / "Quitar filtro: {tag}"), filter_open_cat ("Open {category} filters" / "Abrir filtros de {category}") — both template keys whose placeholders the module substitutes, following the established filter_status pattern.

proposal.title: Filter result motion — sequenced re-entry, spec-sanctioned
proposal.change: When a filter application changes the shortlist, animate the surviving cards' re-entry with a WAAPI sequenced stagger (element.animate, transform+opacity only, ~40ms per-card delay) — motion spec capability S3 ("sequenced timeline… Splice: home hero build; brief evidence reveals" — extended here to the work grid as a principal-visible option, noted as a splice-point extension rather than an invention: the capability itself is sanctioned; the location is new). Panels' open/close uses a compositor-only height-reveal via transform (scaleY on a wrapper with transform-origin top) rather than height animation.
proposal.rationale: Makes filtering feel like curation rather than deletion; showcases S3 on the page recruiters land on first.
proposal.responsive: Identical behavior at all breakpoints; no layout change — motion only.

proposal.title: One new filter category: Status (Live / In progress) — and no more
proposal.change: Add a fourth category, "Status", with exactly two chips: "Live" (cards 1, 2, 4 — pages with real, sourced content) and "In progress" (cards 2, 3 — the badged placeholders; card 2 TUUA is Live-as-work but its page is a placeholder, so its data-tags carry the value matching its PAGE state: in-progress). Implemented purely as data: two data-tag values on chips, data-tags additions on cards, four i18n keys (filter_cat_status, tag_live, tag_wip + ES). The engine needs zero changes — categoryOf reads groups from the DOM.
proposal.rationale: The one category a recruiter actually lacks: "show me only the finished work." It also makes the placeholder state a navigable fact rather than a discovered disappointment — honesty as UX (hard rule: placeholder honesty preserved; this proposal strengthens it). Further categories (stack, year) are deliberately NOT proposed: with four cards, a fourth category is the ceiling before the filter outweighs its pool again.
proposal.responsive: One more trigger in the P-1 bar row; wraps on mobile with the existing flex-wrap. No new breakpoint.
proposal.aa: Same disclosure/chip semantics as P-1; two more chips announced by the existing live region. ES direction: "Estado" / "En vivo" / "En progreso" (usted-neutral labels, anglicismo rule not applicable).

proposal.title: Filter state in the URL hash — shareable shortlists
proposal.change: Reflect active chips into location.hash (#f=banking,frontend-developer) via history.replaceState on apply(), and hydrate from the hash on init. ~15 lines in tagfilter.js; no routing, no storage, no dependency; empty hash = no filters, identical to today.
proposal.rationale: Wave 7's content engine gains deep links ("see my banking front-end work" → one URL). Zero-cost now, compounding value later.
proposal.aa: None regressed; hydration runs before first paint of the grid state, so no announced flicker; hash changes use replaceState to avoid polluting back-button history.

proposal.title: Scroll-progress bar promoted site-wide (the roadmap's named upgrade)
proposal.change: Extract Brief 01's proven progress bar (3px, brand purple, fixed top, grows L→R, reverses on upscroll, aria-hidden="true") into shared files: progress.css under assets/css/shared/, progress.js under assets/js/core/. Home loads both via its existing modular graph (main.js imports + link tag). ARCHITECTURE-ASYMMETRY LANDING: the briefs — self-contained by convention — REPLACE their inline copies with links to the shared files at ../../assets/… — the exact depth-2 relative pattern their i18n CHROME fetches already prove works (IA-CONVENTION's immovable paths untouched). This trades strict self-containment for guaranteed non-drift of a chrome element that must be identical everywhere; the IA convention's own rule ("everything genuinely shared stays shared") supports it — the bar is chrome, not page content.
proposal.rationale: Roadmap-named; unifies the site's most visible chrome signature.
proposal.responsive: Fixed-position 3px bar, viewport-width at every breakpoint; no interaction with any layout.
proposal.aa: aria-hidden="true" (decorative); scroll-linked width update is transform/scaleX-based (compositor-only); under prefers-reduced-motion the bar still tracks position (it is state, not decoration-motion) but its easing transition is removed — matching Brief 01's current behavior.

proposal.target: all pages · assets/css/shared/nav.css + assets/js/pages/home/nav.js + brief inline nav
proposal.title: Smart navbar v2 — active-section awareness + hardened panel semantics
proposal.change: (a) Home: add scrollspy via one IntersectionObserver — the nav link whose section occupies the viewport majority gains aria-current="true" + the existing underline held at scaleX(1). (b) All pages: language panel gains Escape-to-close with focus return and explicit aria-expanded on its trigger (today hover/class-driven). (c) Briefs: no structural change — their inline nav already carries data-nav-context; 6.2 verifies byte-parity of shared behaviors (hide-on-scroll threshold, heights, link set) across the five copies and corrects any drift found, treating nav.css as the single source of truth.
proposal.rationale: Turns the nav from a static header into an orientation instrument on a page that is now five sections deep; closes the one keyboard gap in the language panel.
proposal.responsive: Scrollspy is presentation-only on the existing links; mobile nav behavior unchanged. No new breakpoint.
proposal.aa: aria-current="true" is the canonical current-location semantic; underline persistence gives the sighted equivalent; Escape/focus-return closes the panel per the disclosure pattern; hide-on-scroll already never traps focus (bar returns on upscroll and on focus-within — 6.2 verifies the focus-within clause and adds it if absent).

proposal.title: Unified smart footer — one structure, five pages, zero drift
proposal.change: Canonicalize one footer structure and apply it to all five pages: (col A) tagline + LinkedIn CTA (existing); (col B, new) a compact site map — the four nav anchors plus the four brief links, giving every page a full-site exit ramp; (strip) existing meta plus one new line: the 48-hour response commitment ("I reply within 48 hours." / "Responderé antes de 48 horas." — reusing the established contact-copy fact, no new claim). Briefs receive the identical markup inline (footer is content-light enough that inline duplication is acceptable; 6.2's sweep greps structural parity across the five copies).
proposal.rationale: The footer is the last thing every visitor sees on every page; today it is a dead end on briefs. A site map + response commitment converts it into the site's quiet second conversion surface.
proposal.responsive: Col A/B stack under max-width 767px (existing hinge); site-map links wrap as a two-column list on mobile. Existing footer grid tokens reused.
proposal.aa: Links are plain anchors in a nav element with aria-label="Site" — landmark-correct; contrast from existing tokens; no motion.
proposal.i18n_keys: footer_map_label ("Site" / "Mapa del sitio"), footer_sla (EN/ES above) — CHROME dict, both pages' loaders already consume it.

proposal.title: S1 scroll choreography on Home section entrances
proposal.change: Apply the spec's S1 capability (animation-timeline: view(), pure CSS, @supports-gated, Chromium 115+) to the entrances of the work, capabilities, evolution, track-record, and contact sections — subtle translateY+opacity on section headers and first-level children. Exactly the spec's named Home splice point ("home page section entrances").
proposal.rationale: Home stops being the least-animated page (F-2) using zero JS and the spec's cheapest capability.
proposal.responsive: Identical at all widths; entrance distances in rem.
proposal.aa: Per the S1 contract: static fallback renders rows in place fully opaque outside the @supports gate; reduced motion gets the same static render; no content motion-gated.

proposal.title: S6 restrained depth on work-card hover/focus
proposal.change: The spec's named splice ("home work cards (restrained use)"): preserve-3d + parent perspective, card tilt ≤4° on hover and focus-within, layers at two translateZ offsets (art vs overlay text). Hover-capable pointers only (@media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine) — both queries already in the corpus).
proposal.rationale: The cards are the site's four doors; depth marks them as objects, not rectangles — and demonstrates S6 where recruiters will actually hover.
proposal.responsive: Gated off touch devices entirely; no layout shift (transform-only).

proposal.title: Copy consistency closures
proposal.change: (a) contact_engagement_placeholder: "Selecciona una" → "Seleccione una" (the F-6/5.6 carried item — a one-key ES value fix, in scope here as consistency, distinct from 6.3's parity pass). (b) Brief 01 EN hero_rv_txt "the next four minutes" → "the next five minutes" with ES "los próximos cuatro minutos" → "los próximos cinco minutos" — closing the Wave-4 logged tension in favor of the measured hero_read value, the smaller and factual edit.
proposal.rationale: Two known, logged inconsistencies; both one-line; both voice-preserving.
proposal.aa: None. No fact invented; hero_read's "5 min read" is the measured figure per the parking-lot record.

proposal.title: Breakpoint grid unification
proposal.change: Canonicalize the grid to exactly: max-width 767px / min-width 768px (mobile hinge), max-width 1023px / min-width 1024px (desktop hinge), and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — normalizing the off-by-one variants (768/769 → 767/768; 1024-as-max → 1023) and whitespace variants, file by file. The strays (900px, 641px, 480px) are each individually assessed in 6.2: migrate to the nearest canonical hinge if visually equivalent, retain with a justifying comment if genuinely load-bearing. Every touched file gets a before/after visual check at 360, 767, 768, 1023, 1024, and 1440px.
proposal.rationale: F-4 — the cheapest hardening available; eliminates the 1px dead bands and makes the responsive contract auditable.
proposal.responsive: This IS the responsive-integrity proposal; the six-width check per file is its own regression gate.
proposal.aa: None affected; reduced-motion queries normalized in spelling only, never in scope.

proposal.title: Placeholder heroes sharpened, honesty loudened
proposal.change: On tuua-transfer and limafly-ux only: (a) elevate the in-progress treatment from the current badge to a hero-integrated state line directly under the deck — the existing dashed-purple .temporal idiom, reading the existing hero_status key — so the page's provisional nature is unmissable before any scaffold is read; (b) apply P-5's shared progress bar and P-7's footer like every page. NO scaffold body copy is touched, no badge removed, no figure re-framed — the honesty invariant holds by construction: this proposal makes provisionality MORE visible, not less.
proposal.rationale: The placeholders' current honesty relies on a badge the eye can skip; moving the declaration into the hero's reading path protects both the visitor and the author's credibility.
proposal.responsive: State line wraps naturally; existing hero stack at both hinges.
proposal.aa: Text state line (not color-only); dashed border decorative; existing token contrast.

option.question: Hero signature moment — adopt S5, S3, or neither?

options.option: The motion spec names Home hero for both S5 (compositing sweep — the boldest signature) and S3 (sequenced WAAPI build — replacing the current plain fadeUp cascade). Adopting BOTH would over-animate one viewport. Recommendation if forced: S3 (it upgrades what exists rather than adding a set-piece), deferring S5 to a future refresh. But this is a taste call the principal should make. Either choice ships the capability's static fallback + reduced-motion contract; neither risks AA.

option.question: Evolution timeline — adopt the brief reveal-card pattern?

options.option: Each timeline milestone could carry an aria-expanded reveal ("what this stop really involved") using the briefs' proven rv_btn pattern — progressive depth on the organism recruiters read as a CV. Cost: 6–8 new EN keys + ES, and the timeline gains interaction complexity. Genuinely optional: the timeline works today. Responsive/AA: pattern already proven AA on briefs; would inherit identical semantics.

option.question: P-1 panel behavior on mobile — inline strip or bottom sheet?

options.option: P-1 specifies panels opening as inline strips at all widths (simplest, zero new pattern). A bottom-sheet presentation on max-width 767px would be more thumb-friendly for 13 chips but introduces a new overlay pattern (scrim, scroll-lock, focus trap) the site doesn't otherwise have. Recommendation: inline strips (P-1 as written) unless the principal wants the sheet; both hold AA if built to pattern.

option.question: Status category naming — 'Live / In progress' or 'Shipped / In build'?

options.option: P-3's two chip labels carry positioning weight. "Live / In progress" states page status plainly; "Shipped / In build" reads more product-native but slightly overstates the placeholder pages' trajectory. Recommendation: Live / In progress (the humbler, truer pair). ES direction: "En vivo / En progreso" either way.

enhancement_spec.not_changed: - The filter ENGINE (tagfilter.js matching, dead-end logic, live region) — presentation changes wrap it; the logged faceted-AND tension stays resolved as-is. - The two immovable paths (index.html at root; assets/i18n/{en,es}.json in place) and both i18n loader depths — every proposal was checked against IA-CONVENTION. - Brief 01 and Brief 04 body content, structure, dashboards, and Gantt — the real briefs' locked, sourced material is untouched beyond P-10(b)'s one-word tension closure. - Scaffold body copy on the placeholders — awaiting Waves 2/3 real copy, per the parking lot; P-12 only raises the visibility of its provisional status. - The work-card desktop height clamp and line-clamp safety net from PR-5 — the ~30px residual sizing question above 1024px is a 6.2 verification item, not a redesign. - Zero-build, zero-dependency, hand-authored stack — no proposal introduces tooling. - The ES corpus beyond P-10's two named keys — full ES parity for all new keys introduced here locks at task 6.3, per the roadmap. - The parking lot — read, honored, not actioned; task 6.4 owns it.
enhancement_spec.new_keys: filter_remove_label · filter_open_cat · filter_cat_status · tag_live · tag_wip · footer_map_label · footer_sla · (O-2 if adopted: evo_rv_* namespace, 6–8 keys, HOME body) — EN authored at 6.2 build time per this spec's stated directions; ES locked at 6.3.
enhancement_spec.verification_carryforward: - Runtime check: hero.css animations under prefers-reduced-motion (F-7). - Nav focus-within return on hide-on-scroll (P-6c). - Footer + nav structural parity grep across all five pages after P-6/P-7 land. - Six-width visual regression per file touched by P-11. - The PR-5 lesson institutionalized: any file move or import-path change gets a runtime execution check, not just resolution/existence checks.
